hero: In a provincial hospital clinic in Lucena, Quezon, a Filipino nephrology fellow points to large cystic kidneys on an ultrasound monitor while a 35-year-old Filipino man in a bank teller's uniform and his younger sister look on, a framed family photo held in her hands; warm natural light, thoughtful mood, no text.

figures.teaches: Height-adjusted total kidney volume for age stratifies ADPKD progression and identifies tolvaptan candidates.
figures.content: Graph: x-axis 'Age (years)' 15 to 80; y-axis 'Height-adjusted total kidney volume (mL/m), log scale'. Five fanning bands labeled 'Class 1A', '1B', '1C', '1D', '1E' from lowest to highest growth. Right-side legend with 10-year kidney failure in the Mayo cohort: '1A 2.4%' ... '1E 66.9%' (only the two end values shown, as in the source). Highlighted green box over 1C-1E: 'Rapid progression: KDIGO 2025 tolvaptan if eGFR >=25 (1B); also eligible if eGFR decline >=3 mL/min/1.73 m2 per year'. Footer strip: 'TEMPO 3:4: volume growth 2.8% vs 5.5%/yr | REPRISE: eGFR loss 2.34 vs 3.61 over 1 yr | Everyone: water 2-3 L/day if eGFR >=30 (2D), home BP <=110/75 at 18-49 with G1-G2 (1D), avoid NSAIDs'.

figures.teaches: The affected nephron segment determines potassium, urine pH and urine anion gap in each type of renal tubular acidosis.
figures.content: Nephron outline across the top with three highlighted segments: proximal tubule (type 2), collecting duct alpha-intercalated cell with apical H+-ATPase and basolateral AE1 (type 1), collecting duct principal cell under aldosterone (type 4). Below, a three-column table: rows 'Defect' (cannot secrete H+ | reclaims too little bicarbonate | low aldosterone effect), 'Serum K' (low | low | high), 'Urine pH in acidosis' (>5.5 | can fall <5.5 | usually <5.5), 'Urine anion gap' (positive | variable | positive), 'Clues' (nephrocalcinosis, calcium phosphate stones, deafness in recessive forms | glycosuria with normal glucose, low phosphate | diabetes, CKD, RAAS blockers, trimethoprim). Footer: 'All have a normal plasma anion gap'.
